description:
## Co-organized with NUS Enterprise and TUM Venture Labs

Time to Accelerate Global Defense Innovation:

Join 120+ of the world’s most driven engineers, founders, and operators at the Singapore Defense Tech Hackathon (SDTH) on September 25–27, 2026.

This isn’t a typical hackathon. It’s a premier global launchpad for defense technology. Work alongside  international talent, defense innovators, and industry leaders to tackle real-world security challenges together.

Meet potential co-founders. Build something that actually matters.

Our Mission

Readying the Little Red Dome -

The future of attritable aerial salvos will overwhelm traditional, sequential air defense systems. Revamp these legacy systems with the next generation of technology: With agentic AI, physics & digital twins at its core, compose robust defense products with commercially available technology. Build a new, comprehensive and investable idea that will secure safer skies. Getting sensors, C2, and shooters right is only half the battle. The other half is manufacturing and sustaining low-cost interceptors locally, without being held hostage by export controls or distant logistics chains. Agentic AI, next-generation perception, and additive manufacturing are three parts of the same answer.

Main Category: 2-day Challenge

2-day challenge tracks will be revealed to all registered participants one week before the event. Apply as a Hacker.

Focus Areas

• Autonomous Command & Control (C2)
• AI & Agentic Systems
• Sensor-to-Shooter Integration
• Counter-UAS & Drone Swarms
• Maritime Security & Littoral Defense
• Electronic Warfare (EW)
• Resilient Communications
• Space-Based Infrastructure & Defense
• Modular, Integrated Defense Systems
• “Defense Dome” architectures for city-scale protection

By Invitation Only: 3-Month Extended Challenge

A small number of applicants will be personally invited to take on a 3-Month Extended Challenge - an exclusive track for teams ready to work on problems a weekend cannot contain. Harder, more consequential, and deliberately ambitious. 3-months to work on three open questions to build on our mission, or the domain of your choice, at the  frontier of defense technology:

Track A:

Can we build interceptors fast, cheap, and smart enough to match modern drone warfare, without  skilled pilots or expensive supply chains?

Track B:

Can we design a sensing architecture that holds its picture when hundreds of threats arrive simultaneously?

Track C:

Can we keep meaningful human judgment in the loop when autonomous warfare has already outrun human reaction time?

Track D:

Based on your work and interests, you may also work on deep-tech in the domain of your choice, as long as it is relevant to defense. Do tell us more about your prior experience when you apply as a Hacker.

Selected teams receive mentorship, a per-project budget, and upgraded prizes. Apply as a Hacker. We’ll be in touch.

(You may participate in both the 3-month & 2-day challenges!)

The Prizes:

Prizes worth up to $30,000, including a $12,000 top prize.

SDTH is Phase 1 of a 9-month incubation program through the NUS Defence Tech Venture Lab.

The strongest teams get incubated at NUS with milestone-based funding, mentorship, access to defence testbeds and expert and investor networks.

It is a direct pathway from first prototype to funded defense startup, with roots in Singapore, solving challenges that matter globally.

More details will be shared in June.

name: Claude for Blockchain: Trading Agents
description:
Pre-TOKEN2049 edition · Claude Singapore Community

In March, OKX did something no major exchange had done: they open-sourced a toolkit that lets an AI agent trade directly on their platform. Spot, futures, options, grid bots — 80+ tools, MIT licensed, running locally on your machine.

Most of the industry still hasn't looked at it.

This session is a straight, practical hour on what exchange-native AI trading actually is, what it can and can't do, and what it means for how you work.

What we'll cover

What OKX actually shipped. The Agent Trade Kit, how it plugs into Claude Code through MCP, and the real scope of what an agent can reach — market data, order execution, position management, automated strategies.

The security model, honestly. Your API keys stay in a local config file. The model never sees them. Signing happens on your machine. Why that design matters, and where the remaining risk actually sits.

How people are using it. Research and market analysis, monitoring, strategy testing in demo mode, and execution. Where each one genuinely helps, and where it falls apart.

The part nobody wants to say out loud. AI makes mistakes, and you own the losses. What guardrails look like in practice — read-only mode, demo profiles, permission-scoped keys — and why you should never skip them.

Where the edge goes. When every desk can run the same agent on the same public data, what's actually left worth having.

Then we build one, live

Last fifteen minutes: a working agent wired to OKX through Claude Code, pulling live market data, running in read-only mode. From nothing to working, on stage. No laptops needed — just watch how little it takes.

And then, Pre-TOKEN Networking

Traders, founders, researchers, and anyone doing crypto work who wants to understand this properly before TOKEN2049 week takes over.

name: Collaborative Agent Hackathon @ Stanford
description:
## Build open agents that work together

The Collaborative Agent Hackathon is a one-day event for building open-source, collaborative AI agents using Flower.

Agents are changing what is possible, and their greatest potential emerges when they collaborate safely in human-supervised multi-agent teams.

Participants will form teams on the day, develop a working prototype and present it at the end of the event. Each team will explore how open-source collaborative agents of varying complexity can work together safely.

You do not need an existing team or a fully developed idea. Bring your laptop, your interests and a willingness to collaborate.

## The hackathon challenge

## Build an open-source agent or multi-agent system using Flower in which the safe collaboration of agent teams is central to the solution.

Projects can range across the full collaborative spectrum. Multiple agents might:

• Automate a task
• Form self-improving loops with one another
• Operate across distributed machines and datasets

[Flower](https://flower.ai/) is built together with an open-source community spanning more than 7k users world-wide. Flower simplifies building multi-agent systems, supporting distributed coordination, collaborative learning and inference, and privacy-aware deployment.

Projects from all industries and application areas are welcome — including scientific research, healthcare, finance, education, public services, software development and entirely new forms of human-agent collaboration.

## Team formation

Participants register individually.

Teams of two to four people will be formed during the morning, unless formed earlier. The organisers will help participants find teammates with complementary interests and experience.

Already know your team? Please provide your teammates’ names when registering.

Bringing an idea is optional.

Eligibility: Everyone is welcome, including builders from startups and companies, as well as students, researchers, and postdocs from all universities.

## Awards

Awards will be presented at the end of the day to recognise outstanding projects and contributions.

Further details about prizes and the selection process will be shared before the event.

## Schedule

9:30–10:00 — Opening, check-in and breakfast
Meet other participants and share your interests and experience.

10:00–10:15 — Welcome
Introduction to the event, the challenge and the day’s practical arrangements.

10:15–10:45 — Collaborative agents with Flower
A technical introduction covering collaborative agent architectures, safe coordination, self-improvement loops and the available Flower resources.

10:45–11:00 — Team formation
Meet potential collaborators and form teams of two to four, unless your team was formed earlier.

11:00–12:45 — Build session
Define the project, design the agent interactions and begin implementation.

12:45–1:30 — Lunch

1:30–5:15 — Build session
Develop and test the system, refine the collaboration or self-improvement loop and prepare the demonstration. Mentors will be available throughout.

5:15–5:30 — Demo preparation

5:30–6:45 — Project demonstrations
Teams present their projects, followed by brief questions.

6:45–7:30 — Dinner, awards and closing remarks
Enjoy dinner as we celebrate the winning projects and bring the hackathon to a close.

Singapore and the EU are pursuing distinct but closely watched approaches to digital asset regulation, with both influencing how jurisdictions across APAC develop their own frameworks.

name: TOKEN2049 Singapore. Quantum Security for Digital Assets with Industry Leaders
description:
Quantum Security for Digital Assets

This private technical event brings together industry leaders, protocol engineers, cryptography researchers, digital asset specialists and institutional stakeholders to examine the emerging security requirements of digital assets in a post quantum environment.

The discussion will focus on the cryptographic foundations required to protect digital asset infrastructure as quantum computing develops, including digital signatures, transaction authentication, identity, key management, consensus security and the protection of blockchain execution environments.

Panels with industry leaders will be followed by relaxed networking with senior peers over food and drinks.

Particular attention will be given to the transition from conventional elliptic curve cryptography toward post quantum cryptographic systems and the practical considerations involved in implementing these mechanisms at protocol level.

Topics will include

• Post quantum digital signatures and transaction authentication
• Quantum resistant identity and account structures
• Key generation, address derivation and key lifecycle management
• Post quantum consensus and validator communication
• Cryptographic verification within distributed systems
• Quantum resistant smart contract infrastructure
• Migration considerations for existing digital asset systems
• Security implications for institutional digital asset custody and infrastructure.
• The discussion will also examine how post quantum cryptography can be integrated throughout a blockchain protocol rather than being implemented as an isolated security layer.

Quantova will present its approach to post quantum blockchain architecture, including the Quantova Virtual Machine and its implementation of PQR cryptographic primitives across transaction signing, account creation, consensus and execution.

Attendees will have the opportunity to examine the practical relationship between cryptographic primitives, protocol architecture and application execution, with discussion focused on implementation rather than commercial promotion.

About organizers:

• [Quantova](https://Quantova.org) runs a post-quantum Layer 1 network built from first principles to issue, move, settle and protect digital value: digital identity, stablecoins, tokenised real-world assets, payments and institutional settlement, without inheriting a future migration burden.
• [Quantova launched QDock.io](https://QDock.io), the development environment supporting post quantum application development, together with the underlying cryptographic libraries, compilation tooling and deployment infrastructure used within the Quantova environment.

[Further technical information is available at Quantova.org](https://Quantova.org)

name: Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon
description:
